run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: Datadog APM is not among the data sources available in this run, and the trace and metric backends that are available for target m0-otel-20260909 (Jaeger and Prometheus) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (all trace and Prometheus calls between 17:48:13Z and 17:49:08Z), so no span-level latency could be measured and no single slow downstream call of checkout-service could be identified. Elasticsearch holds no indices (pattern '*' returned none), so no indexed logs could be searched either. What the reachable Kubernetes and pod-log evidence shows does not support a slow downstream call in the requested hour (16:48:13Z-17:48:13Z): in namespace otel-demo all 21 deployments report 1/1 ready replicas and all 32 pods report Running/ready with restartCount 0; checkout logged 24 successful PlaceOrder sequences in which "payment went through" followed the order line by roughly 16-21 ms and "order confirmation email sent" followed about 8-11 ms later, with the same gaps in the earlier part of the hour; payment logged "Transaction complete." about 1 ms after "Charge request received."; email answered POST /send_order_confirmation with HTTP 200 in 0.0028-0.0051 s; shipping created its tracking ID about 5-6 ms after receiving the quote. All 11 flagd fault-injection flags in ConfigMap flagd-config carry defaultVariant "off". The customer-reported checkout slowness is therefore unverified and its location remains a gap, not a finding.

claims.text: In namespace otel-demo all 21 deployments report replicas=1 with ready=1, including checkout (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and payment; the pod inventory shows checkout-6578865d87-v6flf, payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm, cart-549b8757d-7492d, currency-6db8974b78-sk6nq, shipping-6fc5f694db-968zl, quote-75774ddb4c-qq27v, email-6cd97b67f9-tj8fp and product-catalog-777f5468d4-dxh5f all phase Running, ready true, restartCount 0.

checkout logs for the later part of the hour (17:34:17Z-17:47:08Z) show repeated successful sequences of "[PlaceOrder] user_id=..." followed by "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" roughly 16-21 ms later and then "order confirmation email sent to ..." about 8-11 ms after that, e.g. PlaceOrder 17:47:08.104376Z, payment went through 17:47:08.125554Z, email sent 17:47:08.135708Z.

checkout logs for the earlier part of the same hour (17:00:56Z-17:19:38Z) show the same pattern with comparable gaps, e.g. PlaceOrder 17:00:56.007190Z, payment went through 17:00:56.024949Z, email sent 17:00:56.032747Z, and PlaceOrder 17:19:38.598119Z, payment went through 17:19:38.616238Z, email sent 17:19:38.625342Z.

payment pod logs pair every "Charge request received." with "Transaction complete." within about 1 ms (17:30:46.770972Z to 17:30:46.771790Z; 17:34:23.322576Z to 17:34:23.323547Z; 17:47:08.124044Z to 17:47:08.125686Z), all at level info with no error lines in the lines read.

email pod access logs show POST /send_order_confirmation answered with HTTP 200 and request times of 0.0028, 0.0029, 0.0031, 0.0032, 0.0033, 0.0035, 0.0036, 0.0039, 0.0040, 0.0043 and 0.0051 seconds for the 17:38:47Z-17:47:08Z requests shown.

shipping logs show "Received quote: <n>" and "Sending Quote: <n>" in the same millisecond and "Tracking ID Created: <uuid>" about 5-6 ms later, e.g. received quote 17:47:08.119176Z with tracking ID 17:47:08.126093Z, so the checkout-to-shipping exchange completed within milliseconds.
quote pod access log records only "POST /getquote HTTP/1.1" 200 plus a byte count (e.g. "200 5", "200 3") for each request between 17:30:46Z and 17:47:08Z; these lines carry no duration field.

cart logs record ValkeyCartStore calls GetCartAsync, AddItemAsync and EmptyCartAsync with timestamps around each order (GetCartAsync 17:46:31.839659Z and EmptyCartAsync 17:46:31.863647Z; GetCartAsync 17:47:08.059586Z through EmptyCartAsync 17:47:08.128950Z) but contain no per-request duration field.

ConfigMap flagd-config key demo.flagd.json declares 11 flags, every one with defaultVariant "off": productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad (the only latency-style flag, imageSlowLoad, offers 10sec/5sec variants but defaults to off).

The hypothesis that payment (checkout's charge call) is the slow downstream call is rejected for the sampled window: payment logged roughly 1 ms between charge receipt and transaction completion, and checkout's PlaceOrder-to-"payment went through" gap stayed 16-21 ms across the hour.

The hypothesis that the order-confirmation email call is the slow downstream call is rejected for the sampled window: email returned HTTP 200 with request times of 0.0028-0.0051 s, and checkout logged the email line 8-11 ms after the payment line.

The reported slowness may sit in a leg that the application logs do not time - the frontend-proxy/frontend-to-checkout entry call, or checkout's currency-conversion and product-catalog lookups - because no span durations exist in the reachable data; this remains unconfirmed.

Once the Jaeger and Prometheus targets respond for m0-otel-20260909, compare per-operation client-span latency for checkout (span_name/rpc_service breakdown of traces_span_metrics_calls_total or client duration metrics) over the same 60-minute window against a baseline hour, and separately time the frontend-proxy to checkout request, before naming any downstream operation as slow.

gaps: No trace evidence: every Jaeger call in this run (traces_list_services, traces_search for service checkout, including a 17:30-17:45Z window) returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span durations, error tags or parent-child edges for checkout are available.

No span or RPC metrics: get_label_values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, get_metric_names for traces_.*, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so request rate, error rate and per-operation latency for checkout and its dependencies are unknown rather than zero.
No log search index: elasticsearch_list_indices with pattern '*' returned status no_data with zero indices, so no indexed application logs could be searched.

Checkout's call latency to cart, currency and product-catalog is unchecked: checkout logs carry no RPC durations for those legs, currency produced no log lines at all in the window, cart logs contain no duration field, and product-catalog was not read.

The container log stream for the previous instance was unavailable for every pod read (HTTP 400, no previous terminated container), so nothing before the current container instance can be examined; checkout's current container held 297 lines covering only 17:00:56Z-17:47:08Z.

No alert state: whether the configured rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh in ConfigMap prometheus (alerting_rules.yml) was pending or firing could not be checked because list_prometheus_rules depends on the unreachable Prometheus target.
Datadog APM is not among the available data sources in this run and change_history is not integrated, so neither Datadog dashboards/traces nor deployment change history could be used.
The exact downstream identity of the reported slowness remains unknown; no evidence ties any candidate (frontend-to-checkout leg, currency conversion, product-catalog lookup) to the customer report.
next_steps: Restore or confirm reachability of the Jaeger and Prometheus targets, then re-run span latency and span-metric queries for service_name=checkout over the incident hour with a comparable baseline hour.
Compare checkout client spans by rpc_service/rpc_method (cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, payment, email) to isolate which dependency's latency grew.
Check frontend and frontend-proxy request duration for the checkout endpoint, since the request-entry leg is not visible in checkout's own logs.
If Datadog is the intended APM source, connect that integration (or export equivalent span metrics) so the reported customer latency can be measured directly.
Validate the customer report with user-facing checkout latency or SLO data before assigning impact to any service.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

  - action: keep

  - action: replace

    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scheme

  - action: replace
    regex: (\d+);(([A-Fa-f0-9]{1,4}::?){1,7}[A-Fa-f0-9]{1,4})
    replacement: '[$2]:$1'
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_port
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_ip
    target_label: __address__
  - action: replace
    regex: (\d+);((([0-9]+?)(\.|$)){4})
    replacement: $2:$1
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_port
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_ip
    target_label: __address__
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_param_(.+)

  - action: replace

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
